title: Pumpkin Patch Cupcakes
shortDescription: Pumpkin spice cupcakes with a cream cheese swirl and a tiny fondant pumpkin, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These pumpkin patch cupcakes are my go to bake once the leaves turn orange. The cake is soft and spiced with real pumpkin puree, cinnamon, and ginger, so it tastes like fall in one bite. On top goes a tall swirl of cream cheese frosting, piped high like soft serve. I finish each one with a tiny fondant pumpkin so they look like they came straight from a patch. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen to get the spice level right. Too much clove and it tastes like potpourri, so I kept the mix simple and warm. This is an easy recipe for weeknight baking, but it looks special enough for a fall party table.
ingredients: 12 small orange fondant pumpkins with green fondant stems
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice in a bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and brown sugar until fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each one.
Mix in pumpkin puree and vanilla until smooth.
Add dry ingredients in two batches, alternating with the milk. Mix just until combined.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
Beat cream cheese and 1/2 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in batches until fluffy.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, pipe the cream cheese frosting in a tall swirl using a large star tip.
Top each cupcake with one tiny fondant pumpkin and serve.
tips: Use canned pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling, or the cake will be too sweet and wet.
Chill the fondant pumpkins for 10 minutes before placing them, so they hold their shape on the soft frosting.
If your kitchen is warm, chill the frosted cupcakes for 15 minutes before serving so the swirl stays tall.
Make the fondant pumpkins a day ahead so they firm up and are easy to handle.

faq.question: Can I make the fondant pumpkins ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes. Shape them up to 3 days ahead and store them in an airtight container at room temperature so they firm up before topping the cupcakes.

faq.question: Why did my pumpkin cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: This usually means the batter was overmixed after adding the flour. Mix just until you no longer see dry streaks.

faq.question: Can I use fresh roasted pumpkin instead of canned puree?
faq.answer: Yes, but drain it well in a sieve first. Fresh pumpkin holds extra water that can make the cake gummy.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature. Frost and add the fondant pumpkins the day you serve them.

conclusion: These pumpkin patch cupcakes bring fall to the table without much fuss. The spiced cake and cream cheese swirl are a classic pair, and the tiny fondant pumpkin makes each one feel handmade.
